summary: Narrow retest of the iteration-154 bugs, all run in the ISOLATED DB with REAL auth: real FastAPI app over httpx ASGITransport using explicit client peer tuples, real JWT cookies, no auth.current override. The isolated DBs were tejas_isolated_iter155 plus the 154 suite's own DB, and both were dropped. No isolated DB remains, leftover real handles = 0, storage PUTs = 0, and the bridge creds file is deleted. Production and the customer DB were not touched, no owner creds were used, and nothing was deployed. New test_iter155_pin_retest_isolated.py: 12/12 pass. The iter154 suite (already updated by main for the iter155 semantics) passes 27/27 after fixing its audit assert. Limiter results: (a) 70 wrong-PIN requests to different accounts across private peers 10.81.4.212/.213 got no 429, and 65 from loopback got none. Each number still gets 429 on its 6th failure. (b) A public peer (8.8.8.8) gets 429 on its 61st request. Spoofed X-Forwarded-For / CF-Connecting-IP / X-Real-IP / Forwarded headers do not get around this. A different public peer (1.1.1.1) is unaffected, and Retry-After is set. Success clearing: 8 successful logins all return 200. After that, 5 wrong PINs return 401 and the 6th returns 429, and the correct PIN is also 429 during lockout. Legacy profiles stay student in 3 variants (no role/access_type; role=owner + access_type=staff_password; role=reviewer): /me before the change is student with pin_configured=false. The first PIN set returns 200 with the same id and role student, stored pin_version is 1 with a $2b$ hash, and there is only one session row (v1). The old cookie gets 401, a fresh login returns 200 as student, /api/admin/students returns 403 and /api/studio/sets is denied. Cleanup after a PIN change physically removes the old same-user sessions: missing version, v0 and the current v1. It keeps the future v9 row, the new v2 row, another user's v0 row and a staff-plane row with the same user_id. When a PyMongoError is injected into delete_many, the change still returns 200 and the stale row physically remains. Even so, the old cookie gets 401 on /me and /refresh, the old PIN gets 401 and the new PIN 200. Three concurrent changes gave [200,409,409]. A delayed old-version new_session returns 401 and inserts no row, no stale rows exist, and only the winning PIN logs in. Owner directory: sorted by phone, search is correct, and every read adds a student_directory_read row in the actual tejas_audits collection (+2 for 2 reads). ISOLATED PYQ proof: the real reviewed bundle was imported via the owner endpoint (30 papers) with local source PDFs. Two independent cookie sessions (different peers) for the same student ran preflight→start(A)→save(A)→resume(B, same id/deadline, answers visible)→save(B)→A sees both answers→submit(B, 202)→results identical in A and B→original solution PNG read (166404 bytes)→solution-open 200. A reattempt from B created a new blank attempt and the old result stayed unchanged. Both attempts are in history, and another student gets 404. Sanitized ids are in /app/test_reports/iter155_isolated_pyq_proof.json, marked ISOLATED / NOT_NATIVE_OR_PROD_PROOF. Frontend (preview UI with /api routed to the isolated real-auth bridge, port 8793): a signup with mismatched PINs shows 'PINs must match.' and sends 0 signup requests, and a correct signup lands on /home. The Profile Change PIN dialog focuses #change-pin-new (typing goes there), opacity is 1 after settling, and the phone field is readonly. A dialog mismatch sends 0 API calls, a successful change closes the dialog, the old PIN gets 401 and the new PIN 200. Super Admin shows 58 students on 2 pages, both sorted, with p1-last < p2-first; search returns +919815400003 and the empty state works. Privacy copy contains 'The owner can view registered student mobile numbers in a private directory.' No horizontal overflow at 1920x800 or 390x844 on /signup, /profile, /privacy or /super-admin. LIMITATION (not a readiness claim): behind the shared private ingress there is NO per-client-IP limit. Only per-number limits and existing auth concurrency apply until an operator configures trusted proxy headers. This is not evidence of 500k-user readiness. The actual Expo/native app was not available, so no claim of native parity.

minor.issue: A successful login deletes the per-number failure key. If the real owner logs in in between, an attacker gets 5 more guesses per success. Observed: 4 wrong, 1 correct, then 5 wrong all returned 401 with no 429. Low risk (needs the victim to log in), but the 10k PIN space is small. Consider a separate long-window failure counter, or only clearing failures older than the success.

The per-number key is incremented before the IP check. A request rejected by the public-IP 429 still uses up that number's quota, so an attacker on one public IP can lock a victim number for 15 minutes in 5 requests. This is inherent to per-number limits; documented by design.
No per-client IP throttling behind the private ingress until trusted proxy config exists. This is an operator action, not a code defect.

action_items: Optional hardening: keep a longer-window per-number failure counter that a successful login does not reset.
Operator: configure trusted proxy (uvicorn --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=<ingress CIDR>) before claiming per-client-IP protection.
Do NOT deploy the PIN changes until the native Expo client is updated together with them (per user).
critical_code_review_comments: phone.limit_pin: correct to use only the ASGI peer and is_global; it never reads forwarded headers.
change_pin cleanup is version-scoped, plane-scoped and user-scoped; a PyMongoError is caught and logical fencing via check_session_generation remains the source of truth.
new_session for the student plane re-reads the profile and forces role=student, access_type=unverified_phone, so stored role/access_type tampering cannot escalate.
seed_data_creation: Only synthetic data in isolated DB tejas_isolated_iter155, dropped at the end (verified no *isolated* DBs remain).
test_credentials: Ephemeral random synthetic owner/student creds in the isolated DB only; /tmp/iter155_creds.json deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend/tests && python -m pytest test_iter155_pin_retest_isolated.py -p no:cacheprovider -q -n0 -s (about 35s; includes the real PYQ import and the two-cookie attempt proof). Bridge: timeout 2400 python iso_bridge_iter155.py & (port 8793; drops the DB on SIGTERM). In the Playwright route handler, keep a manual dict cookie jar and send a Cookie header: the httpx Cookies jar will not send Secure cookies over http to the bridge, which makes the session look lost after page.goto.
